correctness.rationale: Inclusion-exclusion yields 120S(n,5)=5^n+10*3^n+5-5*4^n-10*2^n, and splitting n=r+2t gives G_r(t)=(5^r25^t+10*3^r9^t+5)/120 plus error -(2^(2n-3)+2^(n-2))/3 of valuation n-2 for n>=5. For s!=t in Z_2, the 25^h-1 and 9^h-1 lifting identities give v2=3+v2(h); their two terms in the difference 120(G_r(t)-G_r(s)) have valuations 3+v2(h) and 4+v2(h), so division by v2(120)=3 yields v2(G_r(t)-G_r(s))=v2(t-s) without possible cancellation. Finite quotients therefore permute every residue separately on each parity. For n>=k+2 the correction vanishes mod2^k and each period 2^(k+1) visits all half-indices modulo 2^k once per parity. Mod-2 pattern (1,1,0,0) excludes odd eventual shifts, and isometry forces all even eventual shifts divisible by 2^(k+1). At n=k+1 for k>=4, the period fails because the correction difference has valuation k-1, proving sharp onset; for k<=3 earliest allowable n=5. Independently generated the Stirling triangle and verified exact balanced parity fibers and onset for k=1..7 and three offset blocks. The all-precision theorem rests on the 2-adic proof, not the checks.
residual_risks: Applies only to fifth column and powers of two; the previously published least eventual period itself is not new.

value.rationale: Complete residue distribution and earliest periodic onset for a natural fixed Stirling column are meaningful arithmetic invariants beyond previously known period lengths and valuations. The fifth column is the first with uniform full binary residue support, and the explicit 2-adic isometry is a structural explanation rather than a finite counting curiosity. A future researcher can use its exact one-per-parity fiber counts and cutoff when studying Stirling congruences.
residual_risks: No conclusion for other fixed columns or odd prime moduli; historical equivalent remains possible.

final_claim: For each k>=1, the Stirling sequence S(n,5) modulo 2^k has least eventual period 2^(k+1) and is exactly two-to-one on every block of that length starting at n>=max(5,k+2), once at each parity, with that starting index optimal. Its parity branches are 2-adic isometric bijections of Z_2; known least period is not asserted as new.
